Welcome to The Breakfast Club. It is not a café, not a shop, not a branch, not a unit, not a restaurant, it is just... a caf. This place is known, not only for their brunches, but also for having food and drink served with a nice, heavy dose of feel-good warmth and hospitality. Google had recommended having breakfast here before starting our day. Needless to say, this was a great recommendation!

My table went with the Eggs All Day and the Short Stack Pancakes. The Eggs All Day is eggs (however you like it prepared) on a thick, buttered, sourdough toast with two or three sides. We went with the bacon, chorizo, and sausage. The eggs were light and fluffy. The bacon was crispy with a slight burnt taste. The chorizo was rich and slightly spicy and a bit tangy.

The Short Stack Pancakes was the main star! We went with the fresh berries, vanilla cream, and blueberry compote as the sides for the pancakes. Each of the sides perfectly matched the pancakes, giving us seven different flavor combinations! Surprisingly, the vanilla cream was not as sweet as I thought it would be. The blueberry compote was also lighter than expected.

If possible, make sure you make a reservation! As this is a small caf, seats are limited. Even if you are a small party, I highly recommend making a reservation.

When I learned that there was a coffee shop just off the beaten path in Soho that just so happens to share the name with my absolute favorite coffee drink I had to check it out.

I arrived 10min before close, so, I wasn't able to really sit in the ambiance that is Flat White. That being said, the staff was friendly, and the service was quick.

Before I talk about the drink experience, some additional details... I fell in love with flat whites when I visited Australia several years ago and I've been ordering and making them at home ever since. One thing worth noting is that a UK (and much of Europe) flat white is not quite the same as an Aussie or American flat white. It's still the same components; rich and bold espresso shot(s) accompanied by textured milk (steam milk infused with air to create a velvety texture), but in the UK they are restricted to cup sizes for some reason (mostly to do with the ratio of espresso to cup size). I was presented with a 4oz to-go coffee cup. The flavor was great, and with execution solid.

While this particular drink was delicious, I think I still prefer an Aussie flat white (or American). Having the barely bigger than espresso size feels like the drink is condensed while I want to enjoy the drink and flavor for longer.

Overhyped, Impressive Presentation, Mediocre Flavours

I visited this establishment after seeing numerous visually appealing reels and photographs on social media. Like many others, I was drawn by its attractive aesthetic.
We ordered three items, all of which were rather average. The presentation and plating were excellent and visually striking, yet the taste fell short of the expectations created by its online popularity. The cakes were ordinary; I have had noticeably better versions from standard UK store bought cakes. The Triple Chocolate Mocha was similarly unremarkable and could easily be made at home.

Items Ordered:
1.  Triple Chocolate Mocha
2.  Double Chocolate Cake with Triple Chocolate Topping
3.  Croissants with Tomato, Cheese, and Basil

Total Bill: £26–30

It was notable that customers at the neighbouring tables also left significant portions of their orders unfinished. In addition, the seating felt quite cramped, with tables placed very close together, making movement difficult and blurring the lines between separate tables.

Conclusion:
I would not recommend this venue and would not return. It may appeal to those primarily interested in attractive surroundings for photographs, but it does not deliver a satisfying experience for those seeking quality food and comfortable dining.

text.text:
Made a comeback to this café after two whole years! It’s such a famous spot that during my last visit, even though there wasn’t a queue, the terrace was completely packed, so I had to take my order to a nearby park. I still vividly remember how beautifully they packaged everything back then, which left such a wonderful impression that I just had to return!

This time, I visited on a Saturday afternoon. The staff took our order downstairs (you pay on your way out!), and we were guided to the upper floor, where we managed to snag a table. The table turnover is surprisingly quick, so people come and go pretty fast. We ordered an English Breakfast tea, scones, and a strawberry cheesecake. The scones were, as expected, absolutely legendary! Having a proper cream tea after such a long time was pure bliss. Another huge plus is that if you need more hot water or milk for your tea, you can just ask the staff, and they’ll top it up right away—we actually asked for a milk refill once. The secret to a perfect scone is the harmony between the clotted cream and strawberry jam, and their clotted cream is incredibly rich and delicious.

But the real hidden gem of the day was the almond croissant we ordered on a whim. Apparently, it’s a low-key favorite here! It was quite big, and the nutty flavor of the almonds paired perfectly with the flaky, crispy pastry. Next time I come back, ordering the scone and the almond croissant together is a non-negotiable. Plus, the atmosphere is so cozy and it’s a fantastic place for a proper catch-up. Such a satisfying visit! ☕️🧁✨

Instagram created too much hype. Although the baked goods were tasty enough, they didn’t quite hit the mark for me. We bought a lot to sample, but nothing really stood out. It was okay. I’m glad I tried it, but this visit was one and done. A more detailed critique of each item is at the end of this review.

We arrived about 15 minutes before opening on a Sunday and there was only one other group waiting outside. Right when the bakery was about to open was when everyone else flocked to the area.

The queuing system is organised. Separate queues for dining in and takeout. If you’re dining in, you receive a table number first before you go to the counter, ensuring that you have a seat waiting for you after you order. We dined in, but they let me order takeout at the same time, which was nice.

Tables are crammed in tightly, so you’re sitting very close to other people. An accessible toilet is available for all to use.

———

Mentaiko shiopan: nice and chewy salt bread with a crispy, crunchy exterior. Good ratio of mentaiko filling. Not spicy, so it was more like tarako. Pretty good.

Wagyu (beef) curry bread: light and crisp deep fried bread containing a decent amount of tasty beef curry, though the onion flavour was pungent. It was minced beef and not chunks of meat, though, so might as well have not been wagyu. Regardless, pretty good.

Layered toast: light and fluffy with excellent lamination, but a little dry and very mild in flavour. Somewhat unexciting.

Black sesame doughnut: delightful enough and not overly sweet, though the black sesame filling was bland and too custardy. Just okay.

Egg tart: Portuguese instead of Hong Kong style. A bit too eggy. Okay, but not exemplary.

Sea salt gianduja cookie: quite bland, since the hazelnut was undetectable and the actual cookie dough itself, if you managed to get a bite without chocolate, was just a flat sweet flavour. Underwhelming.

-86 degree ube latte: good earthiness of the ube, but the drink wasn’t as chilled as expected and it went too far in the savoury territory, making it difficult to enjoy and finish. Definitely wouldn’t order again.

Like so many others, we saw these amazing desserts were trending on social media. And ofcourse, the teenager of our home really wanted to try one of the cute rabbit themed desserts.
Hidden down a beautiful street, we easily found the cafe.
We found the mousses on display in the window, with a brief description of their flavours. I must say, they were every bit as perfect as you see online, and were very, very unique. I can see why they appeal to so many people!
We made our selection, choosing three small mousses, and chose a brown sugar boba milk tea, and decided to eat on the premises. The price for the 3 desserts (no bigger than a rich tea or digestive biscuit - as those biscuits were the base for the mousse) and the 2 boba teas came in at a whopping £39!
Which we felt was expensive, even for London prices!
The cafe itself was OK.... but lacked the wow factor. The walls were unpainted plaster, so had that patchy peach colour. The bench seating was slightly uncomfortable, but did have small round pads to sit on. They just weren't very cushioned!
The desserts were rich but pleasant.
Although I mentioned earlier that the size of them were fairly small, I think they were actually the perfect size, bearing in mind the richness of them.
You certainly couldn't eat a large amount of them, even with a sweet tooth!
But overall, it is somewhere I would recommend trying, mainly for the memories. It isn't the kind of place I would want to go back to. And I think that's probably their general custom. It probably appeals to Londons tourists, those who want to get a cute photo for their social media.
The service was OK. We ordered as we entered, and apart from the staff bringing the food and drinks over, we didn't interact with them any further.
They didnt come and ask if things were OK etc, but we didn't mind that.
There wasn't really an atmosphere of any kind there. I think that they could add some cute decor in theme to their desserts.
As I would imagine that most visitors do take photos for their platforms.
With a little more decor, like themed photo walls, this could create a better vibe.
It was empty when we went in. Only one other table was occupied, a couple with their dog.
That's another thing..... we saw someone walk in, and decide to leave because they had an allergy to dogs.
We actually loved fussing over the dog, but understand not everyone would like a dog near their food!
Overall.... Great for a once only visit. But not somewhere we would go back to.
Photos included to further explain our review. Hope it helps someone 🥰

I was a regular customer at this restaurant when it was Shack Fuyu and always enjoyed the food and great customer service. They have now relaunched as another location for their Bone Daddies chain. I was pleased to find the food and service is as good as ever.

I started off with the Chashu Pork and Katsu Chicken Bao Buns which were both delicious. The buns were well cooked and not too soft. Most importantly, the fillings had lots of flavour and although I enjoyed both, the Katsu Chicken was my favourite.

I then had the Spicy Miso Tonkotsu Ramen, as I like my noodles to have some heat and spice. I used to live in Japan and ramen was one of my favourite dishes. I thoroughly enjoyed the Bone Daddies' take on it. All of the ingredients were cooked well and the sauce was delicious. I could really taste the pork broth and the miso.

The good news is Shack Fuyu's famous Kinako French Toast is now available at Bone Daddies and I recommend leaving some room for it. It really is one of my favourite Japanese influenced desserts in London.

The other good news is the same lovely team are working at this new Bone Daddies and the customer service is up to the same high standard. All of the staff are friendly and helpful and the dishes I ordered were served quickly with no issues.

There are many ramen restaurants in London but I highly recommend giving Bone Daddies a visit. I will definitely continue to be a regular customer to satisfy my craving for ramen.

I recently visited the Boba Bubble Tea store in Chinatown, and unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the most disappointing experiences I’ve had in a long time. I was really looking forward to having a nice refreshing drink, but both of the teas I ordered were completely tasteless and not worth the money at all. I ordered one Milk Bubble Tea and one Passionfruit Fruit Tea, spending around £13 in total, and honestly, it felt like I just threw that money away. The Milk Bubble Tea tasted just like plain water there was no creaminess, no tea flavour, and even the tapioca pearls didn’t help. It lacked that rich, smooth taste that a good milk tea should have. It was so bland that I couldn’t even finish half of it. The Passionfruit Fruit Tea was just as bad. It literally tasted like water with a faint, artificial hint of something sweet, but definitely not passionfruit. It was flat, watered down, and had zero real fruit flavour. I took a couple of sips and left both drinks on the table because they were honestly undrinkable.
I really hate wasting food or drinks, but this time, there was just no point in forcing myself to finish them. The only positive part of the visit was the staff they were friendly, polite, and tried their best to be helpful. It’s not their fault that the drinks were so disappointing, but the quality definitely needs major improvement.
Overall, it was a total waste of money, and I regret choosing this place. For £13, I expected something enjoyable, but instead I got two cups of flavoured water. Definitely not recommended.

I have passed this place many times and been put off by the huge queues.

On a bank holiday, I took the chance to try it as it seemed quiet. However it turned out to be quite stressful on a hot sunny day.
As soon as you walk inside there is a till but no one was there to seve.
The kitchen looked busy and full of staff.

Whilst at checkout on the app I noticed my order was rounded up and I couldnt figure out why, so I left it.
Much later I found out I was charged 20p for a paper bag which I did not need or want.

The app is good to let you know where it is in the queue and to let u know when it is waiting to be collected.
I don't believe they called out my name or number, therefore I had to collect it myself, waving down a staff member.  She was friendly and gave me my drinks.

The mangoes inside the drinks were stringy, I had to spit these out. They were not made with care.
The cups are nice and solid but seems wasteful.
It was also probably the most expensive teas we have had

Overall for us, we did not enjoy the experience of ordering and the carelessness with the mangoes, it was not worth it.

I’ve been a customer of Kissaten since it first opened inside the laundromat. Over the years, I’ve watched it grow in popularity, but unfortunately, the quality of service has declined. Today was the first time I left genuinely frustrated.

The shop is now overcrowded with gacha machines, leaving very little space to stand or move comfortably. A single small service window now handles both gacha and drink orders, resulting in long delays—especially when someone places a large gacha order. During my visit, around ten drink orders appeared to be stalled with no visible progress. Several customers voiced their concerns, but the staff seemed largely indifferent.

After waiting for about 15 minutes, we were informed that our drink was unavailable—something that should have been communicated at the time of ordering. No apology or compensation was offered. When we asked for a refund and expressed our frustration, the staff member told us we were “holding her up.” We weren’t given any proof of refund, only a verbal confirmation.

It’s disappointing to see a place I once really enjoyed become so poorly managed. What used to feel welcoming and efficient now feels disorganised and dismissive toward customers.

As for the gachapon machines, they feel questionable at best. My sister visited a few months ago and received the exact same keychain twice in a row—of the least popular character. Recently, I spent £6 on a broken Sanrio toy that didn’t even light up as advertised. It’s hard not to feel that the odds or quality aren’t quite as they should be.

The boba itself is decent but nothing special—certainly not enough to justify the experience or the prices.

Overall, Kissaten remains a cute and aesthetic stop in Soho, but at this point, it’s more style than substance. Sadly, it’s no longer worth the money or the frustration.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Very Late Review – Glad I’m Finally Posting This! Amazing Bubble Tea in Chinatown

I’ve been meaning to leave this review for ages and I’m so glad I can finally do it now. One late evening after spending the whole day exploring Chinatown with a few friends, we decided we needed some bubble tea before heading home. We popped into Yunique Bubble Tea and it was the perfect way to end the day.

I got the strawberry bubble tea and it was genuinely very nice refreshing, full of real strawberry flavour, and perfectly sweet. What really stood out was the size!These drinks are seriously large and they are not stingy at all with the portions. You get a proper generous cup filled with drink, not half ice and disappointment like some other places. The pearls were chewy and fresh too. They have a great variety of teas to choose from, all with vibrant colours that look super appealing and make it hard to pick just one.

The place has a lovely vibe bright, very clean, and well kept. The staff were nice and friendly, which made the quick stop even better.

Address: 10 Little Newport St, London WC2H 7JJ

Big disclaimer (nothing to do with the shop itself): If you’re driving, do NOT try to drive around Chinatown and central London, especially in the evening. I made that mistake and it was crazy – so many people everywhere on the roads and pavements, barely any space to move. Parking is an absolute nightmare. Please take the train or tube for your own peace of mind, unlike me!

All in all, Yunique Bubble Tea is a fantastic spot for high-quality, generous bubble tea in the heart of Chinatown. Fresh, tasty, and great value. I’d happily go back anytime. Highly recommended!🧋✨

Just visited Wuye Bubble Tea during PandaGo's promotion (spend £5 save £4) and it was absolutely worth it! This is hands-down one of the best bubble tea spots in London Chinatown.

🍹 MUST-TRY DRINKS:
- Passionfruit Trio – An explosion of fresh passionfruit seeds with just the right balance of tartness and sweetness. The jasmine tea base elevates the flavor, and the combination of coconut jelly, crystal boba, and tea jelly makes every sip exciting.
- Berry Braggart – Made with real crushed strawberries and peach resin (Tao Jiao), this drink is both refreshing and lightly floral. A hint of rose salt enhances the natural berry sweetness.

☕ TEA BASE HIGHLIGHTS:
- Their  Premium Black Tea has a deep, caramel-like aroma (UVA high-altitude leaves).
- The Four Seasons Green Tea is subtly floral with a touch of osmanthus—so fragrant!

🍮 DESSERT WINNER:
The Crème Brûlée  is UNREAL—thick caramelized crust with ultra-rich custard made from clotted cream. Best I’ve had in London!

⏰ Pro Tip:Go before 3 PM to avoid long waits.

Final Verdict: 10/10 for quality and flavor. Even without the discount (£5-£4 deal until March 28), it’s worth every penny!

Really enjoyed my visit to Pot and Rice in Soho. The place has a nice, modern vibe and feels relaxed even when it’s busy.

The highlight for me was the foie gras & Chinese sausage claypot rice — and they were very generous with the foie gras (two big pieces!). The foie gras was nicely seared, rich and buttery, and the oil soaked into the rice perfectly. Great smoky flavour from the sausage and crispy rice at the bottom, full of wok-style aroma.

Also tried the kimchi beef claypot rice, which was bold and comforting — tangy, slightly spicy and very satisfying. The foie gras & roe rice rolls were smooth and indulgent, and the starters like salt & pepper chicken and jellyfish shredded chicken were solid and well executed.

Desserts were a nice surprise too — the French toast and mochi were soft, rich and a great way to finish the meal.

Overall, a great spot for claypot rice in London, especially if you’re looking for something a bit different from the usual. Would happily come back. 👍

TeaKnows - Authentic Chinese Tea Experience in London

Tucked away near Tottenham Court Road station at 112 Great Russell St, TeaKnows offers one of the most authentic Chinese tea experiences I've found in London. This charming teahouse has quickly become my go-to spot for quality tea drinks.

The star of their menu is undoubtedly the Linlan Latte (£5.8/6.2). The robust black tea base pairs perfectly with the creamy topping, creating a smooth, caramel-like flavor when mixed. I particularly enjoy the hot version on cooler days - it brings out the tea's natural warmth and depth.

For something more refreshing, the Zimo Green Tea (£4.8/5.4) is excellent. The jasmine green tea shines through beautifully, especially when ordered with less sugar. It's light yet flavorful, with a lovely floral aroma.

Their Osmanthus Rice Wine Tea is truly special. The sweet osmanthus fragrance hits you immediately, followed by the subtle complexity of rice wine. It's a unique combination that's perfectly balanced - not too sweet, with just enough complexity.

Additional highlights:
- They sell premium tea leaves in beautiful packaging
- Knowledgeable staff who clearly care about tea
- Traditional Chinese decor that creates a peaceful atmosphere
- Convenient location near the British Museum
- Open until 10pm, great for evening visits

What sets TeaKnows apart is their commitment to authentic flavors. The teas taste natural and well-balanced, without relying on excessive sweetness. You can tell they use quality ingredients and proper brewing techniques.

While the space is small, it's always clean and welcoming. The staff are happy to explain the different tea options and make recommendations based on your preferences.

For anyone looking for genuine Chinese tea drinks in London, TeaKnows is absolutely worth visiting. It's become my favorite place to enjoy a moment of calm with excellent tea.

Rating: 5/5
Address: 112 Great Russell St, London WC1B 3NQ
Nearest Station: Tottenham Court Road (3 min walk)
Hours: Daily until 10pm
